lead.headline: Changes to high-risk medical devices filed as 30-day notices, skipping full FDA review, rose from 19% to 64%
lead.number: 19% of approval changes in 2000-04 to 64% from 2010 on; one Medtronic defibrillator line (P980016) has 928 changes, 621 of them 30-day notices.
lead.watch_out: No skeptic has checked it; long-lived pacemaker and defibrillator lines pile up manufacturing changes, and the device-problem reports here cover only 2020-01 to 2021-09.

sources.quote: The most common supplement type was 30-day, at 7250 (67.3%), while PTS was least common, making up 132 (1.2%) of all supplements.
Excluding 30-day notice supplements, which have increased markedly since their introduction in 1997, there was still a 3-fold increase over the past decade, from 60 supplements to 194.
These PMAs were the subject of 5829 PMA supplement applications. Nearly half (2754, 47%) were approved as 30-day notice supplements for manufacturing changes.
The study found that the most-used supplement type is a 30-day notice, used when a company makes changes to a manufacturing procedure or the way it makes a device.
Almost all, 99%, of the supplements were filed without clinical data.
Two brands of cardiac defibrillator leads (Sprint Fidelis [Medtronic] and Riata [St Jude Medical]) were recalled after being approved by supplements due to high rates of lead failures.
